四级汇总词汇 · 03英文原文

The Table Where People Could Talk

能听清谈话的那张桌子 · 649 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A community center invited older residents to a Sunday brunch downtown, mostly for conversation. The manager, Ruth, set a long dining table in the main hall. There was a buffet, a coffee booth, and music from powerful speakers. Soon an elderly guest moved into the quiet courtyard. He could hear the bass from the lounge, but he could barely follow a conversation with the person beside him. Ruth had reserved the best table for him. She had paid attention to the view and forgotten to ask whether people could hear there.

2A waitress carried his mug outside. A regular diner at the pub had raised the same annoyance. Loud music and the roar of a blender covered speech. One diner had yelled for a pancake while his neighbor tried to ask for a takeaway. Ruth walked down the aisle and read a line from a specials board. At the rear her voice returned as an echo. Diners among tightly packed chairs had to lean sideways. In that arrangement a passive guest could hardly join in.

3A student brought a portable recorder and activated the center's console. Its dual receiver could utilize multiple channels, but Ruth wanted a simple test. A microphone picked up a line about the chef's vegan menu. One channel carried the words clearly. The other held dishes, voices, and laughter. The student tried automatic dictation. Its failure in the noisy room convinced him that impressive gadgetry could not fix the problem on its own. He modified the arrangement rather than increase the volume.

4In the courtyard a smoky barbecue and a breezy corner made the recorder hard to use. Ruth chose shade beside a wall. A fizzy drink rattled on a tray whenever the door shut. One volunteer blamed the excited crowd. Another said a loose hinge was obviously striking the frame. The waitress put cloth under the tray instead. The intense noise eased. Guests could occasionally hear the bar. They could still laugh loudly without breaking up every conversation. Ruth asked the student to note which change had made the equipment responsive enough.

5The chef could offer hearty soup, spaghetti, and a toasted sandwich without using the mixer. The waiter served a decaf latte and a cappuccino with a straw. A guest sipped his drink while a member of staff dialed down the music. A vegan diner ordered grilled vegetables, appreciative of being able to speak without shouting. They moved karaoke to the hall after midday, leaving the patio for a leisurely chat. That change let the center entertain one group while giving others the pleasure of a quiet meal.

6A volunteer recently put up a screen. "Frankly, folks need room," she said. She eagerly turned it so a handful of residents could try sitting behind it. The surroundings felt pleasant when the blender no longer dominated the conversation.

7After lunch Ruth asked everybody for one brief remark. One resident praised the attentive waitress. Another said the silence at first had made her suspicious. She had expected an argument about who should leave. Once they could speak clearly, she recalled the name of the old pub and offered to bring a photograph. A younger guest took a picture of the table and asked whether they could use the same spot for a video call with relatives abroad. The manager saw that the change had made more kinds of interaction possible.

8At the next gathering Ruth greeted him at the entrance. He declined the reserved seat and headed straight for the courtyard. She had left a chair there, angled so he could see each speaker's face. He placed his mug on the cloth and began to tell a story. By the end of it, three people had pulled their chairs closer. The hall still offered plenty to enjoy. This was the place where a guest could finish a sentence and hear what the next person said.

四级汇总词汇 · 03中文译文

能听清谈话的那张桌子

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1市中心一家社区中心邀请老住户来吃周日早午餐，主要是让大家聊聊天。经理露丝在大厅摆了一张长桌，现场有自助餐、咖啡摊，还有大功率音箱放音乐。很快，一位老人走到安静的院子里。休息区的低音他听得到，身边的人在说什么却很难听清。露丝给他留了自认为最好的桌子，只顾看景色，没问那里能不能听清别人讲话。

2女服务员把他的杯子端到外面。酒吧的一名熟客也抱怨过这件事。高声的音乐和搅拌机的轰鸣盖住了说话声。有人大声点煎饼，旁边的人则想问能不能外带。露丝沿过道走了一趟，读了特价板上的一行字。走到后排，回声传了回来。椅子挤得太紧，食客只能侧着身子说话，比较安静的人就更难参与。

3一个学生带来便携录音机，打开中心的调音台。双路接收器能用多个频道，露丝只想先做个简单测试。麦克风收到了一句关于厨师纯素菜单的话。一条音轨里能听清每个字，另一条混着碗盘声、人声和笑声。学生试了自动听写，在嘈杂的屋子里没能识别出来。他这才明白，再花哨的设备也不能单独解决问题，于是先改座位和设备的摆放。

4院子里烤肉的烟和阵风干扰录音，露丝挑了墙边的阴凉处。门一关，托盘上的气泡水就叮当响。一名志愿者怪人群太兴奋，另一人觉得是松动的铰链在撞门框。女服务员给托盘垫了块布，响声就小了。客人偶尔还能听到酒吧，却能放声笑几声而不打断每一桌的谈话。露丝请学生记下究竟哪一步让设备能顺利收音。

5厨师不用搅拌机，也能提供实在的汤、意大利面和烤三明治。服务员端来低咖啡因拿铁和一杯配吸管的卡布奇诺。有客人慢慢喝着，工作人员把音乐音量调小。一位纯素食客点了烤蔬菜，很高兴不用喊就能让人听见。他们把卡拉 OK 移到午后大厅，露台可以留作慢慢聊天的地方。喜欢唱歌的有了活动时间，其他人也能安静吃饭。

6一位志愿者最近立起一块屏风。她直截了当地说，大家总得有点空间。她把屏风转了个方向，请几位住户试着坐到后面。搅拌机不再盖住谈话，四周舒服多了。

7午饭后，露丝请每人简单说一句。有人夸服务员细心，另一人说起初那么安静，她还怀疑大家要为谁该离开而争吵。等到能听清彼此的话，她想起旧酒吧的名字，说下次带张照片来。一名年轻客人拍下这张桌子，问可不可以坐在这里和国外亲人视频通话。露丝意识到，这个改变还让更多交谈成为可能。

8下次聚会，露丝在门口招呼那位老人。他谢绝预留的座位，径直走到院子里。露丝在那里斜放了一把椅子，方便他看清每个说话人的脸。老人把杯子搁到布上，开始讲故事。讲到最后，已有三个人把椅子拉近。大厅里依然热闹，院子里的客人也能把一句话说完，听见下一个人的回答。
